thread:
maria_g: Heads-up — getting a sudden spike of 502s for tenant `acme-corp` hitting the hosted inference endpoint. Happens when their client sends our merged `X-Client-Meta` header. Upstream log shows 'upstream prematurely closed connection'.

jon_k: Can you paste a sample request (sanitized) and the trace id?

maria_g: Trace ids: `t-9f3a`, `t-9f3b`. Sample header (sanitized): `X-Client-Meta: user=alice;session=xxx;features=...` — but it's very long, often >12k bytes.

ingress-bot: env0/frontdoor-12 | 2026-02-18T14:03:22Z | id=t-9f3a | ERROR upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream

alice_r: We shipped header-merge optimizations last week — we collapse multiple small client headers into one to reduce request count. Might be concatenating without trimming.

jon_k: Could be hitting Envoy/NGINX header buffer limits and causing the upstream to drop? Usually that's a 431, but if upstream can't handle stream could yield a 502 from frontdoor. Reproable with a long header?

maria_g: Yes, I repro'd locally with this curl: 
```
curl -v -H "X-Client-Meta: $(python -c 'print("a"*13000)')" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer redacted" \ 
  https://api.hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Result: immediate 502 from frontdoor.

sre-luca: Attach of the frontdoor logs shows the same pattern: connection resets while forwarding to runtime pool. I'm leaning toward upstream worker OOM or read buffer exhaustion. Any recent runtime mem changes?

alice_r: No runtime mem changes. The only relevant change: the header merge logic now leaves the combined header unbounded. Should have capped, but bug skipped the cap for `X-Client-Meta`.

devex-emma: Customer reported this as "request failing and seeing timeouts in our app" — they're starting an escalation. They also saw token/billing errors because retries double-billed some calls. Need a quick mitigation.

jon_k: Mitigation options: 1) revert header-merge canary, 2) add a per-request header length check at the edge that returns 4xx to clients (better than 502), 3) increase buffer limits on frontdoor (fast but risky). Which is fastest?

alice_r: Reverting canary is fastest and least risky. We can roll back the merge change on the two frontdoors in the canary pool in ~10m. That will stop new long combined headers. We'll follow with an edge-side guard to reject >8k headers with 431/400.

sre-luca: I'll stand by for rollback and monitor error rates + runtime pool health. Set alerts on frontdoor 502s and runtime OOMs.

maria_g: I'll draft the repro steps and include the curl snippet and traces, then open a follow-up ticket for adding the header-size validation in ingress.

devex-emma: I'll message the customer with an interim note: "we've identified an issue with header aggregation causing 502s; mitigation underway; will update in 30m."

jon_k: After rollback, please paste the post-rollback graphs (5m/1h) and we'll decide if we need to increase frontdoor buffers temporarily.

ingress-bot: rollback job started: canary-frontdoors -> revert commit `89a7f2` (header-merge). ETA ~8m.

maria_g: Thanks — monitoring now. 502 rate dropping on canary frontdoors (prelim).

sre-luca: Confirmed — t-9f3a/t-9f3b traces show successful 200s after rollback. We'll keep the canary rolled until patch adds a hard cap and unit tests.

alice_r: Plan: ship patch that caps merged header to 8k, add unit tests, and add ingress guard to return 431 with clear message. Then we can re-enable with monitoring.

devex-emma: I'll send the customer the update and offer to run a header-trimming client-side script if they need help.

maria_g: Filing internal follow-up: postmortem template, attach traces + curl repro + PR for cap.

jon_k: Nice work collab. :thumbsup:

ingress-bot: rollback job finished: success

sre-luca: I'll leave the monitoring dashboards on for 24h and export the error aggregation to the incident channel if anything reappears.

alice_r: Added TODO: improve docs for header-merge behavior so customers know limits.

maria_g: Closing this thread after postmortem draft.

:thumbsup: reactions from jon_k, devex-emma, sre-luca
